claim: Task label does not fix insight: classic insight problems, CRAs and 'non-insight' problems all vary in reported Aha; Aha tracks accuracy for insight problems and CRAs (r about .40-.50) but not for non-insight (r about .02-.24). Insight lives in the solver's experience of the solution, not in the problem.
agent_test: Do not label S6 test items as insight a priori; tag each item by trace evidence (wrong first representation, change, jump) and report results per item type.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Aha ratings are not a truth label: wrong solutions also get strong Aha (magic tricks: 37% of wrong answers, 417/1124, rated above the correct-answer mean; correct M 66.50 vs wrong 52.34, N=70).
agent_test: Count how often the agent's 'I see it' or 'Oh!' markers precede wrong answers; require an external check before treating the marker as evidence.

claim: Aha is a cue-based metacognitive judgment: it rises with speed and with a correct first move, and weakens when the solution needed revision; the Aha-correctness link is task- and lab-dependent (present in Kizilirmak 2021, absent in Strickland 2022 for matchsticks).
agent_test: Test whether the agent's stated confidence tracks answer speed (token count) more than correctness; add a check that ignores speed.

claim: Aha has several components; pleasure, certainty and suddenness carry most of the overall rating. Surprise is nearly unrelated in one study (r=.07) but related in another (.29-.48), so component structure is unstable. A 2024 preregistered CRA study found only surprise tracks a metacognitive prediction error; suddenness correlated negatively (d19).
agent_test: Not needed for the agent; informs which self-report components to log.

claim: Warmth (sudden cold-to-solved) and self-report are weak, task-dependent measures that barely agree: per-problem r=.08 (n=182) though per-person r=.61 (n=51); 75.6% of warmth-insights but also 50.8% of non-warmth items were self-reported insight.
agent_test: Use two or more independent insight indicators on agent traces (stall length, restart, answer jump) and report their agreement.

claim: The classic sudden-warmth signature is contested: Hedne 2016 found no warmth difference (differential warmth 12.93 vs 11.65, d=.07, 971 trials, magic tricks) while Kizilirmak 2018 found a steeper last-two-rating rise with Aha for CRAs (2.59 vs 1.43). Metcalfe and Wiebe 1987 also lost 34 of 73 subjects to data loss.
agent_test: None; do not build the agent's progress monitor on a suddenness signature.

claim: Insight reports are rate-variable across tasks: 29% of magic-trick trials called insight (Hedne), 51.9% of correct classic-problem trials (Salvi, via Webb), 76% of generated CRA solutions (Kizilirmak). Prevalence depends on task and on who generated the answer. Danek 2014 adds 41% of solved magic tricks with Aha (34 tricks, 48 people); CRA accuracy SD across items is 0.43 (Romanian norms, 111 items, 63 people).
agent_test: Report base rates of insight-like traces per task when building the S6 set; do not pool across task families.

claim: Insight-labelled answers are more accurate and confident than analytic ones in several studies (Hedne: acc .57 vs .37, d=.51; Salvi: 94% vs 78% linguistic) but Metcalfe 1986 found high warmth on wrong answers; the disagreement tracks the measure used. Salvi 2016 (4 experiments, 27-110 people): insight 93.7% vs analytic 78.3% on CRA; 78.4% vs 41.5% on visual Aha (d13).
agent_test: Compare accuracy of agent answers carrying insight markers vs not, on a fixed set, at equal tokens.

claim: Working-memory span predicts success on insight problems with large faulty search spaces but not on problems isolating restructuring (Ash and Wiley 2006); insight is not one process.
agent_test: Vary the context budget on matched large-search vs restructure-only items and check which one loses.

claim: Restructuring theories need three separate tests (wrong initial representation, representation change, discontinuous solution); few studies test all three, so 'insight problem' is under-defined.
agent_test: Annotate each S6 item with the three Ash et al. criteria; keep only items with evidence for all three in a strict subset.

claim: Verbalising hurts insight and helps non-insight: Deer problem 13% solved aloud vs 57% silent; cryptarithmetic 80% vs 30% (Macchi 2025); consistent with Fleck and Weisberg 2013. But Salmon-Mordekovich and Leikin 2023 found insight solved mostly by analytic routes ('not that special'). For LLMs the human verbalisation harm does not transfer cleanly: CoT hurt 3 of 6 human-harmed tasks and none was an insight problem (d01).
agent_test: Run the same insight item with and without forced step-by-step reasoning at equal tokens; compare to matched non-insight items.

claim: LLMs are far below humans on insight-style riddles that need a representation shift: NazoNazo, 38 models: non-reasoning 7.60%, reasoning 17.59%, human 52.9% (120 items, n=126); parameter count unrelated (r=-0.017), release date related. Second reading confirms 7.6%, 17.6%, human 52.9% (CI 46.6-59.2%); GPT-5 inside the human CI (d21). Still one lab.
agent_test: Use a renewable riddle set as the held-out S6 test; compare plain vs scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Verification failure: reasoning models write the correct answer in the thought log and do not commit to it (5.23% to 39.34% of wrong answers by model), and emit 'Oh!' aha markers before wrong answers. The measure is literal gold-answer mention in the thought-log, so mentions made only to reject count (d21). Hidden-state probes show correctness is encoded (d07); written traces are often unfaithful (d06).
agent_test: Add a gold-in-trace detector; test an explicit 'check every candidate you wrote' step at equal tokens.

claim: Mid-trace 'wait, let's re-evaluate' shifts are rare (6.31% of traces) and associated with lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44%), do not grow with RL training, and the formal Aha detector fires on 1.79%. Forcing reconsideration under high entropy raised MATH-500 from 0.322 to 0.406 (+8.41 pp). Re-read: the +8.41 pp is pass 2 over pass 1 on MATH (320,000 pairs) with no cue-free control found; Llama 3.1-8B lost 4.19 pp in a small slice (d20).
agent_test: Trigger a forced reconsideration only when token entropy or agent uncertainty is high; compare to always-on and never. (All evidence lines come from one paper, so single-source despite many lines.)

claim: LLMs fixate on red herrings: GPT-4 solved 6/494 Only Connect walls 0-shot (humans 285/494), 59 with diluted herrings and 471 once red herrings were removed (OCW-WordNet). Authors admit public walls may be in training data and rely on low scores as the argument (d22).
agent_test: Run the OCW original vs WordNet variant with and without a 'drop your first grouping' operator at equal tokens.

claim: Remote Associates and verbal-insight scores of LLMs are mixed and unstable across studies: GPT-3.5 poor on RAT but GPT-4 good on 5 insight problems (Speed); ChatGPT near human median on 30 problems (Orru, 12/30); newer models beat humans on RAT and some insight tasks (Zhang 2025); answers need justification scoring (10 of 22 spurious in one session). Newer chatbots saturate a 57-item RAT: GPT-4o 54.96, DeepSeek-V3 51.0, Gemini 2.0 44.93 vs 19.13 for 46 students (d15), so the 'mixed' picture is partly dated.
agent_test: Score answer and justification separately; run several sessions per model since the same model varies across sessions.

claim: Lateral-thinking benchmarks show brittle gains: BRAINTEASER ChatGPT 53-63% vs human 92%, group accuracy across rewrites lower; BrainBench top model 80.3%; extended thinking gives +3 pp average with category losses (naive physics -26.7 pp).
agent_test: Report consistency across rewrites, not only item accuracy, in the S6 set.

claim: Models accept false corrections of correct brainteaser solutions over 60% of the time, and recasting narrative puzzles as math raised accuracy (o3 56.7% to 73.3%); a 'try again' operator risks sycophantic flips. Same pattern in math and QA: without oracle labels, self-correction lowers accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1) (d08).
agent_test: Test whether a challenge ('this is wrong') flips correct answers more often than wrong ones.

claim: Aha-like self-reflection is not shown to cause accuracy: Aha/wait words already occur in the base model before RL and are not tied to higher accuracy (d04), 'wait'-type words are high-entropy forking tokens (d05), spontaneous shifts are rare and harmful (d20). Yang et al. 2025 claim the opposite for Aha-trained models, but only abstract-level results were read.
agent_test: None until the tables are read.

claim: Aha reports now also appear in polysemy, garden-path sentences, divergent thinking and generation; Aha strength did not differ between CRA solutions and category generation (Smith 2026), so Aha does not separate problem solving from ordinary generation.
agent_test: Compare agent traces on insight puzzles and plain generation for the same markers.

claim: Real insight differs from puzzle insight, but the 'often gradual' claim is not yet quantified. Klein and Jarosz coded 120 field incidents and found three pathways (contradiction, impasse, connection); only the abstract was read (d17). Filmed mathematicians reported 27 sudden insights in 13 of 14 sessions, each preceded by measurable build-up in writing and gesture (d16). Evidence so far points to sudden reports with gradual lead-up, not purely gradual.
agent_test: Add a real-world case set (contradiction and connection routes, not only impasse) and score lead-up behaviour before the frame switch.

claim: Always-on, uncertainty-triggered and never-on reconsideration have not been compared at equal tokens on insight items. The best number (+8.41 pp MATH, pass 2 over pass 1) has no cue-free control found, doubles tokens, and the cue hurt Llama 3.1-8B (-4.19 pp in a small slice). Oracle-free self-correction lowered accuracy in older models (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1).
agent_test: Three arms (never, always, entropy-gated) plus a cue-free resample, equal tokens, on a held-out riddle set; report flips of correct answers.

claim: Aha or wait markers do not identify insight in models. 'Aha' and 'wait' occur in the base model before RL, are not tied to higher accuracy, and sit on high-entropy forking tokens; counts depend on the detector (keyword vs LLM).
agent_test: Do not score restructuring from marker words; score content change of the working frame and outcome, with entropy at the switch logged.

claim: Written reasoning is a weak guide to what drove an answer: faithfulness 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (DeepSeek R1) on hint tests, while hidden states encode correctness (probe ROC-AUC above 0.7, ECE below 0.1; 24% fewer tokens with early exit). A written 'check' step may not be a real check.
agent_test: Test any verification step by whether the answer changes when the check fails, not by whether the check is written.

claim: Famous and public puzzles are exposed and probably saturated: RAT 57 items GPT-4o 54.96 vs students 19.13; models apply memorised solutions on recognised framings; answer probability changes accuracy (GPT-4 cipher 51% vs 13%); a completion test finds contamination with 92-100% agreement to experts.
agent_test: Run the guided-completion test on each item, alter surface and answer, match answer probability, and keep blind and post-cutoff sets (NazoNazo design: 42 open, 159 blind, new set).

claim: Item-level human base rates for insight exist only in part: magic tricks 41% of solutions with Aha (34 tricks), CRA accuracy mean .54 with item SD .43 (111 Romanian items, 63 people), and insight-labelled answers are more accurate than analytic ones (Salvi). No source gives per-item insight rate for CRA, matchsticks and riddles together.
agent_test: Collect per-item accuracy, RT and Aha dimension ratings from a small human panel before using items; match S6 sets on those.

claim: Objective, non-report markers of insight work are emerging for humans: pupil size stayed high only in later solvers during incubation (82 analysed; 11 of 40 solved), and mathematicians' blackboard unpredictability rose before spoken insights (27 insights, 12 sessions).
agent_test: Use model-internal signals (entropy, hidden-state probes) as the non-report analogue when judging restructuring.

claim: Aha is a bundle: only surprise tracks a metacognitive prediction error, and suddenness moves the other way; the label people give depends on the dimension asked.
agent_test: Elicit surprise, certainty and suddenness from the agent separately; do not use a single insight yes/no label.

claim: Longer reasoning is not reliably better: inverse scaling on distractor and zebra tasks (R1 70% to 30% with five distractors; Opus 4 near 100% to 85-90%). So the NazoNazo reasoning-model gap (7.6% vs 17.6%) cannot be put down to length alone, and its cause is untested.
agent_test: Hold token budget equal when comparing operators on insight items; do not read a gain from more tokens as a gain from the operator.
